thesis.company_overview: Tenet Healthcare Corporation is a US healthcare-facilities operator — sector Healthcare, industry Medical Care Facilities — whose model monetizes acute-care hospital admissions and outpatient/ambulatory surgical procedures through contracted reimbursement from commercial and government payers. It is not a manufacturer; value accrues through facility utilization, payer rate negotiation and cost discipline rather than product IP, which makes the revenue line a function of volume, acuity mix and reimbursement policy. On a TTM basis the business generated $21.812 billion of revenue, with FY2025 revenue of $21.310 billion and FY operating income of $3.508 billion; the balance sheet carries $30.676 billion of assets against $21.976 billion of liabilities, leaving $4.658 billion of stockholders' equity — a capital-intensive, leverage-bearing structure typical of facility operators and the reason the DCF's WACC anchors at 6.24%. A segment revenue breakdown was not available for this issuer; see the latest annual report for business-line detail. Geographic revenue split was likewise not sourceable — no country-level revenue figures were provided — though the issuer reports in USD and its filings describe US operations. The durable moat rests on local market density — clustered facilities that drive physician referral and payer-contracting leverage — plus scale-driven procurement and an outpatient footprint that shifts lower-acuity volume off the higher-cost hospital campus. That structure supports the model's 3.3%/yr average FY revenue-growth fade and 3.0% terminal growth, but does not immunize the operator from reimbursement-policy cycles, which is why terminal growth is held at long-run nominal GDP rather than a premium rate.
thesis.competitor_analysis: Peer screening returned no usable comp set for this ticker this run, so we cannot cite peer valuation multiples or quantify relative market share — that absence is a data-fetch/coverage gap for this run, not a property of the industry. Qualitatively, Tenet competes in a fragmented, reimbursement-driven facilities market where scale, local density and payer contracting — not product differentiation — decide margin, and hospital operators, ambulatory-surgery platforms and physician-group peers are not interchangeable and should not be judged on one multiple. Because neither a subject nor peer trading multiple was supplied, we deliberately avoid any peer-relative premium/discount conclusion and rest the valuation view on the DCF band of $549.05–$915.09 against the $266.91 market price. The competitive takeaway is structural: moat durability here depends on reimbursement and utilization, which is why the model holds terminal growth at 3.0% rather than a growth premium.

thesis.narrative:
We initiate Tenet Healthcare Corporation (THC) at Buy. The one valuation method that ran this cycle is a 10-year DCF that discounts a revenue-growth fade averaging 3.3% per year — 3.6% in FY1 declining to 3.0% by FY10 — at a 6.24% WACC with a 3.0% perpetuity rate applied after the explicit window, producing a mid output of $732.07 and a published band of $549.05–$915.09. The stock trades at $266.91, so the entire DCF range sits above the tape; the BUY therefore reads off the nearest published range bound ($549.05), not the withheld interior point.

The gap is wide enough that we withhold a point target rather than stamp false precision on it: the lone DCF mid of $732.07 is 2.7x the $266.91 market price, outside the [0.5x, 2x] single-method calibration band. The reverse-DCF is the reality check. Holding the model's 6.24% WACC fixed, the market implies ~-4.9% per year of revenue decline held constant across all 10 forecast years; holding growth fixed, it implies a ~9.46% discount rate. These are single-variable solves, not a joint forecast, and a flat -4.9% rate is a different construct from the model's declining 3.6%-to-3.0% fade averaging 3.3%/yr — but even the market's own solve asks only that Tenet shrink roughly 5% a year, which is plausible-but-bearish for a $21.812 billion TTM-revenue operator, not an impossibility. That asymmetry is why the direction is Buy while the magnitude stays unpublished.

Catalyst support is thin but real: Tenet raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance on 2026-10-06 (impact score 5), the only positive item in the feed. Running the other way, insiders were net sellers of [target withheld] over 90 days with [target withheld] of open-market purchases, anchored by a [target withheld] sale by CEO Saumya Sutaria, and 13F coverage of just 7.4% leaves ownership too thin to assert conviction. Momentum is constructive — +40.5% over one year, 87% of the 52-week range — leaving only 5.7% of drawdown cushion. Net: the fundamental floor justifies the Buy, while the insider distribution warrants monitoring rather than abandonment.
thesis.news_summary: Sentiment across the 30-day window (feed items dated 2026-09-08 to 2026-10-10) is bullish at a +0.58 net catalyst score, but it is concentrated in a single event: Tenet's 2026-10-06 upgrade of full-year 2026 revenue guidance (impact score 5), the only positive item the feed surfaced. The remaining coverage is low-signal — 10 SEC 8-K filings in the index, split across 'other' (3) and 'management' (2) categories, with no negative catalyst recorded and no other event carrying a scoring impact. Directionally this supports the thesis: an operating beat-and-raise is consistent with the model's 3.3%/yr average FY revenue-growth assumption and with the +40.5% one-year price return. It does not, however, corroborate the DCF's far-above-market band — nothing in the news flow explains why the $266.91 tape should sit 2.7x below the $732.07 DCF mid output. Net, news supports the Buy direction while leaving the magnitude of the valuation gap unvalidated.

thesis.valuation_overview: Only one valuation method ran this cycle — a 10-year discounted cash flow — so the implied prices do not diverge across methods; they are a single method's output, not a weighted blend. The DCF discounts a revenue-growth fade averaging 3.3% per year (3.6% in FY1 declining linearly to 3.0% by FY10) at a 6.24% WACC, with a 3.0% perpetuity growth rate applied after the explicit window; that yields the method's mid output of $732.07, which the synthesis brackets with a ±25% single-method confidence dial into a published band of $549.05–$915.09. No peer comp set was produced for this ticker this run and no dividend-discount or other method was computed, so there is no second leg to weight against the DCF and no weighted-average price was formed. The point target is withheld rather than averaged: the $732.07 DCF mid is 2.7x the $266.91 market price, outside the [0.5x, 2x] single-method calibration band, and publishing it would stamp false precision on a lone, far-from-market estimate. The band still supplies a fundamental floor, with direction taken from the market-implied reverse-DCF — a ~9.46% implied discount rate or ~-4.9%/yr implied growth versus the model's 6.24% WACC and +3.3%/yr average fade.
